title: Student can later deny having submitted the assignment
description: If the submission action is not bound to the student's authenticated session with adequate evidence (for example, no reliable submission receipt, weak audit trail, or no integrity-protected timestamp), the student may plausibly repudiate having uploaded the file or claim a different file/version was submitted.
assumptions: The portal may rely on basic login state alone and may not generate tamper-evident submission records or receipts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort based on standard LINDDUN repudiation structure; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Submission traffic can link the student to a specific course and assignment activity
description: The transmitted data and communication metadata together associate the student identifier with a course, uploaded work file, and submission time. If observed in transit or via network metadata, this can link the same student across submissions and academic activities.
assumptions: An observer may access transport metadata, endpoints, timing, or insufficiently protected payload data.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may differ in the local LINDDUN Pro tree; linkage via communication metadata is the intended grounding.

title: Submission data in transit can identify the student

title: The submission reveals sensitive academic behavior and content

assumptions: Assignment contents may contain personal data or unique writing patterns; timing may reveal behavior such as lateness or study habits.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; disclosure of content and behavioral metadata is clearly applicable.

title: Portal may disclose submitted work and metadata beyond what is necessary

assumptions: The portal stores submissions and metadata and may make them accessible to multiple roles or downstream systems.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate; threat is grounded in recipient-side overexposure after collection.

title: Portal may use the submission for secondary purposes incompatible with the student's expectations
description: After receiving the assignment and metadata, the portal or connected services could use them for plagiarism-model training, analytics, profiling, retention beyond course needs, or other secondary purposes not expected by the student.
